key_insight: Photonic variational circuits are trainable when the observable’s sample variance does not collapse faster than the circuit variance, enabling polynomial-cost optimization for fixed-order photon-number measurements.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical rule for choosing measurement observables in photonic quantum hardware so gradients and loss changes can be estimated with feasible shot counts.
method: Define trainability by the ratio of sample variance to circuit variance.
Analyze photon-number observables to separate polynomial-cost and exponential-cost regimes.
Compare quantum estimation against classical methods and identify neural-network observables as an efficient readout strategy.
evidence_signal: The paper combines analytic results with numerically observed polynomial decay of circuit variance to show fixed-order photon-number polynomials scale polynomially in samples, while high-order polynomials and output-probability observables typically scale exponentially.
watch_item: The favorable scaling depends on staying within specific observable classes, so implementation choices in measurement design can quickly move a circuit into a non-trainable regime.
paper_title: The trainability of photonic quantum circuits
